title: When the Postcard Wakes
premise: Cyrus Vane, a single parent who rebuilt their life after testifying against the Harrow family's corrupt shipping empire, has spent seven years hiding behind the counter of the town's only bookshop, comforted by anonymous letters from an unknown ally. When the letter-writer—Marlowe Ashe, once the Harrows' inside lawyer who turned evidence and vanished—moves in next door, Cyrus realizes the family's remaining power has followed them both to this coastal town. As the last ferry of the season approaches, Cyrus must choose between fleeing again or staying to help Marlowe expose the Harrows through a trial no court will touch, ending with justice delivered outside the law and the two of them choosing to stay after the last train leaves.
about_author: Lior Thornbury is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who writes slow-burn romances about people rebuilding lives from wreckage. They live on a windswept coast where the ferries genuinely stop running each winter.

chapters.title: The Tenth Letter
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. On the anniversary of the testimony that broke the Harrow empire, a tenth unsigned letter arrives—and Cyrus spots its author carrying boxes into the empty house next door. Marlowe Ashe, the lawyer who vanished after turning witness, is living twenty feet away. The emotional beat is vertigo: seven years of careful invisibility collapsing in a single afternoon.

chapters.title: What the Ferry Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Cyrus and Marlowe. Forced proximity over borrowed sugar and shelving repairs becomes confession: Marlowe reveals the Harrows' surviving heir, Dorian, has bought the town's harbor lease and is quietly buying silence again. Cyrus's daughter befriends Marlowe, raising the stakes. The emotional beat is reluctant trust kindling into something warmer and more dangerous.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Ash
chapters.summary: Marlowe's POV, then shared. Marlowe recovers the hidden ledgers proving Dorian's new corruption, but Dorian retaliates—Cyrus's bookshop lease is revoked and a fire guts the back room. With the last ferry departing in three days and Cyrus packed to flee with their daughter, the emotional beat breaks at the climax: Cyrus chooses to stay, handing the ledgers to the town assembly because no court will hear them.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Shared POV resolving into Cyrus's. At the town meeting, the ledgers turn the harbor workers against Dorian, whose own crew delivers him to the mainland authorities—the ferry he meant to control carries him away instead. The season's last train leaves without them; Cyrus asks Marlowe to stay. The emotional beat is quiet triumph: justice won outside the law, and love chosen over escape.
